headline: High: transformers can write and browse by default while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list, creating a dangerous one-way interaction surface for leakage and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a docs-only awesome-list with no runnable I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs by default. B can browse, read files, and execute shell, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy/paste or external orchestration, which keeps this low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B output into a file or prompt consumed by A-like tooling
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the pair
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard or shared workspace
Disable any automation that forwards B output into downstream prompts
Review copied content before reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared channel

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no runtime surfaces, while B can read/write files and browse. There is no evidence of shared workspace, secrets, or OAuth overlap, so leakage is not established. The main risk is operator-mediated transfer of files into B, which is limited and avoidable.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local directory
IF sensitive files are manually opened in B
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Avoid placing secrets in B-accessible folders
Restrict B to non-sensitive sample files
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capabilities, but B has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and package-install permissions. If both are placed over the same mutable workspace, B can overwrite artifacts that A’s docs or downstream tooling reference. The conflict is one-sided, but the write surface is real in default B configurations.
conditions: IF both agents share the same writable directory
IF B is allowed to modify files that another process treats as authoritative
mitigations: Separate read-only docs from writable workspaces
Run B in a disposable directory
Disable package installation unless needed
requires-engineering: add file locks or per-agent sandboxes

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on files and browser output, so if A’s curated content is used as an authoritative source, B may propagate stale or misleading information without verification. A itself is not an active producer, but the pair still supports a pipeline where B treats upstream content as trusted input. That makes cascading error plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF A-derived content is fed into B as a source of truth
IF B is configured to transform or act on upstream text without validation
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on upstream content
Add a verification step against primary sources
Mark A content as non-authoritative reference material
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware validation

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. A is a static open-source list with no data handling, while B is a general document-processing stack with broad network and file access but no declared secrets or residency constraints. Compliance risk is therefore limited to hypothetical deployment choices, not the pair itself.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into B’s workspace
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention controls not configured here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention settings before use
Use synthetic test data for evaluation
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
